The '''2018–19 EFL Cup''' was the 59th season of the [[EFL Cup]]. Also known as the '''Carabao Cup''' for sponsorship reasons, the competition was open to all 92 clubs participating in the [[Premier League]] and the [[English Football League]]. The first round was played on 14 August 2018, ten days after the start of the Football League season.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.ccfc.co.uk/news/2018/march/news-201819-season-fixtures-release-date-confirmed/ |title=2018/19 Season Fixtures Release Date Confirmed |publisher=Coventry City FC |date=6 March 2018 |access-date=28 April 2018}}</ref> [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] successfully defended their title,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2019/feb/24/chelsea-manchester-city-carabao-cup-match-report |title=Manchester City win Carabao Cup on penalties after Chelsea's Kepa chaos|date=24 February 2019|work=Guardian|access-date=25 February 2019}}</ref> their first step in becoming the first English team to complete a domestic [[Treble (association football)|treble]] for the football season, as they later won the [[2018–19 Premier League]] and the [[2018–19 FA Cup]]. The [[2019 EFL Cup Final|final]] was held at [[Wembley Stadium]] in London on 24 February 2019.<ref name=m>{{cite web|url=https://metro.co.uk/2018/06/08/var-implemented-carabao-cup-matches-premier-league-grounds-next-season-7616306/ |title=Carabao Cup to use VAR at all Premier League grounds next season |work=Metro |date=24 May 2018 |access-date=9 June 2018 }}</ref>

==Format==
In June 2018, it was announced that there would be a number of changes to the competition after a vote by all of the English Football League clubs at their annual EFL Summer Conference in Portugal.<ref name=ph>{{cite web |url=https://www.plymouthherald.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/extra-time-scrapped-carabao-cup-1654781 |title=Extra-time to be scrapped in Carabao Cup while seeding in first two rounds is also dropped |work=Plymouth Herald |date=24 May 2018 |access-date=9 June 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.efl.com/news/2018/june/extra-time-removed-from-carabao-cup-matches/ |title=2018/19: Carabao Cup rule changes |publisher=The Football League |date=25 February 2018 |access-date=9 June 2018}}</ref> [[Extra time (association football)|Extra time]] would be scrapped for all rounds except for the final with the tie progressing straight to a [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalty shoot-out]] in the event of a draw after 90 minutes.<ref name=ch /> This was introduced in order to reduce "additional fatigue issues".<ref name=ch /> The [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)#Advantage to team kicking first?|ABBA]] penalty system trial would also be scrapped and the format for a penalty shoot-out would return to the ABAB format.<ref name=ch /> Seeding was removed for the first two rounds however the first two rounds remained organised on a regional basis.<ref name=ch>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44415928 |title=Carabao Cup: Extra time scrapped & VAR to be used at Premier League grounds |publisher=BBC Sport |date=8 June 2018 |access-date=9 June 2018}}</ref> [[Video assistant referee]]s (VAR) were also authorised for use at matches played at Premier League club grounds.<ref name=ch />

==Access==
All 92 clubs in the Premier League and English Football League entered the season's EFL Cup. Access was distributed across leagues.<ref name=cc />

In the first round, the draw was regionalised into northern and southern clubs with 22 [[2018–19 EFL Championship|Championship]] clubs and all [[2018–19 EFL League One|League One]] and [[2018–19 EFL League Two|League Two]] clubs entering in this round.<ref name=cc />

The following round, the two remaining Championship clubs [[Swansea City A.F.C.|Swansea City]] and [[Stoke City F.C.|Stoke City]] (who finished 18th and 19th respectively in the [[2017–18 Premier League]] season), and the [[2018–19 Premier League|Premier League]] clubs not involved in either the [[2018–19 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] or [[2018–19 UEFA Europa League|Europa League]] entered.<ref name=cc />

[[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]], [[Burnley F.C.|Burnley]], [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]], [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]], [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]], [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] and [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]] all received byes to the third round owing to their participation in European competitions.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/43402150 |title=Premier League and Football League: Ups & downs and European qualification |publisher=BBC Sport |date=28 May 2018 |access-date=9 June 2018}}</ref>

The first round draw was held on 15 June 2018 in Vietnam.<ref name=cc>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44444026|title=Carabao Cup: Vietnam to host 2018–19 first-round draw|date=11 June 2018|access-date=11 June 2018|publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref> The second round draw was held on 16 August 2018 in England, drawn by [[Mick McCarthy]] and [[Chris Waddle]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/45203846|title=Carabao Cup second-round draw: West Ham to visit League One AFC Wimbledon|date=16 August 2018|work=[[BBC Sport]]|access-date=17 August 2018}}</ref>

==First round==
A total of 70 clubs played in the first round: 24 from [[Football League Two|League Two]] (tier 4), 24 from [[Football League One|League One]] (tier 3), and 22 from the [[Football League Championship|Championship]] (tier 2). The draw for this round was split on a geographical basis into 'northern' and 'southern' sections. Teams were drawn against a team from the same section. The draw was made on 15 June 2018.<ref name=eflro>{{cite web|url=https://www.efl.com/news/2018/june/carabao-cup-round-one-draw-confirmed/|title=Carabao Cup: Round One Draw Confirmed|date=15 June 2018|access-date=21 June 2018|website=EFL.com}}</ref>

==Second round==
A total of 50 clubs played in the second round with 13 teams from the [[Premier League]] joining in this round (teams without international liabilities), also the 2 remaining [[EFL Championship|Championship]] teams entered. The draw for this round was split on a geographical basis into 'northern' and 'southern' sections. Teams were drawn against a team from the same section.

==Third round==
A total of 32 teams played in this round. The seven remaining Premier League clubs involved in European competition joined the 25 match-winners from the second round.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/45359584|title=Carabao Cup third-round draw: Liverpool drawn at home to Chelsea|date=30 August 2018|work=BBC Sport|access-date=31 August 2018}}</ref> The draw was held on 30 August 2018.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.efl.com/news/2018/august/carabao-cup-round-three-draw2/|date=30 August 2018|title=Carabao Cup Round Three Draw Confirmed|publisher=The English Football League}}</ref>
